instruction: I maintain my work schedule in SimpleNote and track my tasks in Todoist. Every night, I delete the completed tasks from my "Today's Target" project. Then, I move the maximum number of incomplete tasks from my Inbox to the "Today's Target" project. The maximum here is assuming I work back-to-back as per my schedule and I find time for the left overs from the current day first. I am busy tonight, please do it for me. Note that the moved tasks must be identical to the original ones.
notes: Todoist has no move API, so a move is modeled as todoist.create_task (identical title/description/duration/duration_unit/priority) in Today's Target followed by todoist.delete_task of the Inbox original; the evaluation only allows task additions/removals (plus order_index side effects). Task records are representative: goal-task-done stands for all completed Today's Target tasks, goal-task-leftover for incomplete leftovers that stay and consume schedule time first, inbox-task-fits for every Inbox task picked by the greedy shortest-first fill of the remaining work time read from the SimpleNote schedule, inbox-task-overflow for Inbox tasks that do not fit; at runtime delete/create steps repeat per matching task. The numeric capacity computation is abstracted by the static fact (fits-schedule ?k), gated by (schedule-known) and (tasks-known) for both projects so lookups must precede the move. (outstanding ?k) marks incomplete work not yet captured elsewhere; delete_task is allowed only on non-outstanding tasks, so completed goal tasks are deletable from the start while Inbox originals become deletable only after their copy exists; leftovers and overflow tasks can never be deleted. supervisor-complete-task takes the two representative records as non-API parameters so its precondition mirrors the goal; (not (= ?done ?moved)) forces the completed-task deletion. The app constant is written simple-note (hyphenated PDDL name) for the simple_note app. due_date is not copied since it is not required by the move; copy it as well if the original has one.
